name: Factory
h1: Factory ARR: ~$50M for Droids That Own Engineering Tickets.
intro: Factory builds agent-native software development — autonomous "Droids" that take a ticket, write the code, run the tests and open the review, with enterprise guardrails. Tracking services put its run rate around $50M roughly ten months after the platform took off, and Leonis Capital charts it among the fastest AI companies to that mark. The reported numbers are below.

modelTitle: Sell Finished Tickets, Not Copilot Autocomplete.
modelParagraphs: Factory's bet is that the valuable unit of software work is the finished ticket, not the suggested line. Droids take an issue from the backlog, work it autonomously — code, tests, migration scripts — and open a review when done, with enterprise permissions and audit trails wrapped around every run. That positions Factory against engineering headcount rather than against editor plugins, a much larger budget line.

Revenue is enterprise platform contracts: a base platform fee plus usage as Droid runs scale across an organization's repositories. Because agents work inside existing CI and code review, expansion follows visible output — the same dynamic that made code assistants spread bottom-up, but priced against completed work.
revenueMix: Enterprise base fees for deploying Droids across repositories.
Pricing that scales with the volume of agent-completed work.
Permissions, audit and compliance tiers for regulated engineering orgs.

faqs.a: Around $50 million, estimated. Factory has not disclosed revenue; ARR Club tracks the run rate and Leonis Capital charts the company at roughly ten months from public launch to $50M ARR. Treat the figure as an estimate.

Factory's autonomous software engineering agents. A Droid takes an assigned ticket, writes the code, runs the tests and opens a pull request for human review — operating inside enterprise permissions and audit trails rather than as an editor plugin.

faqs.q: How Is Factory Different from Cursor or Copilot?
faqs.a: Copilots autocomplete inside an editor with a human driving. Factory agents own tickets end-to-end in the background — the buyer's frame of reference is engineering capacity, not seats of an IDE, which is why it sells as platform contracts with usage.
Matan Grinberg and Eno Reyes founded the company in San Francisco in 2023, with early backing led by Sequoia, to make agents the primary interface for software development.
Enterprise platform contracts with a base fee plus usage as agent-completed work scales. Compliance and audit tiers add on for regulated organizations.
